name: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
problem: Conventional wisdom says speculative decoding only helps at SMALL batch sizes, so it is useless in the high-throughput serving regime that production actually runs in.
mechanism: Analyses how the bottleneck SHIFTS as batch size and sequence length grow: at small batch decode is bandwidth-bound (speculation helps), but at large batch and long context the KV CACHE becomes the binding constraint. Attacks the KV bottleneck directly by running the DRAFT MODEL with a SPARSE KV CACHE, which scales with sequence length and batch size while the target keeps a dense cache. Adds a theoretical model that selects the optimal drafting strategy for a given configuration rather than a fixed one.
speedup_reported: Up to 2.51x speedup for Llama3.1-8B at batch sizes 32 to 256 for moderate-to-long sequences, on various hardware and task types. This is the record that makes the batch-size caveat falsifiable: the batch sizes 32-256 are stated, and the gain is claimed precisely in the regime where the field had assumed speculation would not help.
notes: ADOPTION: research-only - the sparse-KV draft-model idea is not in production engines. VENUE NOTE: no venue verifiable via Semantic Scholar, no arXiv comment venue, so venue = arxiv-preprint and year = ArXiv v1 (Aug 2024). This paper is the CORRECTIVE to every batch-1 speedup in this sub-area, and is the record to cite when someone quotes 2.7x-6.5x from Leviathan/EAGLE/EAGLE-3 without a batch size: at batch 1 that is real, and MagicDec shows a different and smaller gain mechanism is available at batch 32-256 where the batch-1 result does not transfer. The honest reading is that these are two different operating points, not competing claims. Also note 'various types of hardware' in the abstract - the per-hardware attribution is not recoverable from the abstract, so hardware_relevance lists accelerator families the class of work uses rather than a per-configuration attribution.
